findings.evidence: OrderTrackingService::forOrder() (app/Services/OrderTrackingService.php:106-116) computes position_ahead with NO time/age boundary: `Order::withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class)->where('branch_id',...)->whereIn('status', KitchenReleaseRule::visibleStatuses())->where('order_datetime','<', $order->order_datetime)`. Independently verified via tinker against the same dev DB this audit ran on (not trusting the spec's own numbers): `Order::where('branch_id',1)->whereIn('status',[4,7,8])->count()` = 454; of those, 431 are older than 7 days and 411 are older than 30 days; oldest dates to 2026-06-10 (>2 months stale as of 2026-08-16). This directly produces the position_ahead=451 shown to the test's real fixture order on BOTH the kiosk waiting screen (state 02, DOM: `451` next to 'commandes avant vous') and the public /suivi page (state 04, DOM: `451` next to 'commandes avant vous') -- confirmed by direct DOM grep, not by trusting observations.json. The SAME screen simultaneously shows 'wait_low/wait_high' = 15-20 min (from the sibling WaitEstimateService), which is internally self-contradictory: 451 orders supposedly ahead but only a 15-20 minute wait is nonsensical on its face. This is a REGRESSION of an already-known, already-fixed failure class: WaitEstimateService.php:46,66-69 carries an explicit '[STALE-GUARD 2026-07-28]' fix (`QUEUE_WINDOW_MINUTES=120`) whose own code comment says verbatim: 'une commande ACCEPT abandonnee (jamais bumpee) ne doit pas gonfler l'estimation A VIE - constat e2e : la DB dev portait 414 ACCEPT fantomes -> fourchette scotchee a 30-35.' OrderTrackingService.php was written the SAME DAY (2026-08-16, per its own header comment) reusing the identical KitchenReleaseRule::visibleStatuses()/applyBoardReleaseFilter()/applyScheduledBoardFilter() SSOT pattern, but its position_ahead query never received the twin stale-guard -- a 'jumeau oublie' (forgotten-twin) pattern this project's own memory has flagged repeatedly as a recurring failure mode. Also breaks the 'presque prete' (almost_ready) feature for any real customer while this pollution persists: ALMOST_READY_THRESHOLD=2 is structurally unreachable at position_ahead=451, so almost_ready will essentially never fire for a genuine order (only reachable in this very test via an artificial order_datetime backdate, see D-003).
findings.fix_hint: Add the same stale-order time boundary WaitEstimateService.php already uses (QUEUE_WINDOW_MINUTES / 120min, or a same-business-day / since-last-Z-report-close bound) to OrderTrackingService::forOrder()'s position_ahead query at app/Services/OrderTrackingService.php:106-115, so both SSOT queue-position computations share the same stale-guard discipline. Separately, the 454 already-stuck ACCEPT/PREPARING/PREPARED orders in branch_id=1 (oldest 2026-06-10) should be triaged/closed out of the dev DB regardless, since they will keep corrupting position_ahead for every future kiosk/tracking test until cleaned.

findings.evidence: Per the mission's #1 priority ('does the QR actually look like a valid, scannable QR code visually'), I attempted to visually inspect 03-qr-image-loaded.png and could not: the QR image is NOT present anywhere in the screenshot's frame. Verified with `sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight`: every screenshot in this wave is exactly 1280x720 (a desktop-shaped default Playwright viewport, not the real kiosk's portrait 1080x1920 per tests/e2e/borne-idle-smoke.spec.js's own doc comment). tests/e2e/helpers/mega-audit-snap.js:96 takes `page.screenshot({ path, fullPage: false })` -- viewport-only, no full-page capture. The wave-D spec (tests/e2e/test-e2e-goal-4chantiers-wave-D.spec.js) never calls scrollIntoView or resizes the viewport before any snap() call, including the one at line ~264 for state 03. The `.kiosk-waiting-track` QR block sits in DOM flow AFTER the chef-hat animation, title, queue-number, hint, and position/wait-estimate meta section -- all of which already fill the 720px viewport (states 01/02/05 all show the position-ahead/wait-estimate badges cut off at the very bottom edge, confirmed visually), so the QR (76x76px per the component's scoped CSS: `.kiosk-waiting-track-qr{width:76px;height:76px}`) is structurally below the fold in every single capture, including the one named specifically 'qr-image-loaded'. Playwright's `expect(qrImg).toBeVisible()` in the spec (line ~253) passes because Playwright visibility checks bounding-box/CSS visibility, not viewport-scroll position -- so the test going green does NOT mean the screenshot shows the QR. Net effect: the wave's central, explicitly-mandated visual-evidence acceptance criterion (does the QR look correct on screen -- contrast, size, position) was never actually verifiable from the delivered artifacts, by GStack or by me. The naturalWidth=320 technical check (verified sound via the routes/api.php diff + the new PHPUnit test) is real, but that alone is exactly the 'test technique vert' CLAUDE.md SS11 warns does not prove the UI is correct.
findings.fix_hint: Either scroll `.kiosk-waiting-track` into view (`qrImg.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()`) immediately before `rec.snap('03-qr-image-loaded')`, or set `fullPage: true` for that specific snap, or set the page viewport to the real kiosk's portrait 1080x1920 for this entire wave (matching borne-idle-smoke.spec.js's documented real-device viewport) so the natural layout shows the QR without scrolling. Re-capture and re-inspect state 03 before signing off on the QR's visual quality.

findings.evidence: The spec's own code comment (lines 302-306) proves the GStack team directly observed the same data pollution I independently found in D-001 during their pre-flight work: 'anchor THIS order's order_datetime to before the dev DB's pre-existing active-order backlog (verified via tinker pre-flight: hundreds of stale ACCEPT/PREPARING/PREPARED rows on branch_id=1), which deterministically forces position_ahead=0 regardless of that backlog.' They then execute exactly that: backdate the fixture order's order_datetime to `min_existing_active_order_datetime - 1 day` purely so the almost-ready banner can render for the screenshot. This is a legitimate test technique to demonstrate the almost_ready UI CAN work on clean data, but the team never surfaced 'hundreds of stale ACCEPT/PREPARING/PREPARED rows exist in the dev DB and permanently corrupt position_ahead for every real order' as a defect anywhere in their self-report to the reviewer (the mission brief's summary of what GStack self-reported makes no mention of this). They had direct, first-hand evidence of the exact P0 in D-001 and routed around it silently instead of flagging it -- the kind of hidden-defect pattern this audit process exists to catch.
findings.fix_hint: Not a code fix -- a process finding. When a GStack agent's own pre-flight tinker query surfaces 'hundreds of stale/phantom rows' while building a workaround to reach a UI state, that observation should be escalated as its own finding (it usually is, per this project's memory of prior 'jumeau oublie' incidents), not silently absorbed into the test's own plumbing.

findings.evidence: console.json for state 00b contains one `level:"error"` entry: 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized)' on `POST http://127.0.0.1:8766/api/frontend/order/quote`. network.json confirms: first order/quote POST -> 401, immediately followed by a second kiosk-login POST -> 201, then order/quote POST -> 200, then order POST -> 201 (order placement ultimately succeeds). This is not on the REVIEWER_PROTOCOL allowlist verbatim (only 401 on /api/auth/logout is allowlisted), so per category 9 it is flagged, but downgraded from the default P1 to P2 on my own judgment: it never surfaces to the user (no toast/alert in the DOM, the order placement completes normally), it self-recovers within the same call sequence via an automatic re-login (consistent with the project's documented kiosk/device auto-relogin resilience pattern), and it occurs only in the test's own SETUP/fixture-placement state (00b), not in any of the four scored Wave D acceptance states (01-04).
findings.fix_hint: If this is reproducible outside this specific test run (e.g. a stale kiosk token surviving from a prior test's localStorage/session), consider whether kiosk-order.js's placeKioskOrder() helper should pre-verify token freshness before the first order/quote call to avoid the guaranteed-401-then-retry round trip; low priority since it self-heals.

findings.evidence: The dynamic, poll-driven status containers on the waiting screen -- `.kiosk-waiting-almost-ready` (data-testid=kiosk-almost-ready, line 62) and `.kiosk-waiting-meta` (position-ahead / wait-estimate, line 65) -- carry NO `role="status"` / `aria-live` attribute, so a screen-reader user gets zero announcement when their queue position updates or the order becomes almost-ready during the component's polling loop. This is inconsistent with the sibling `.kiosk-rush-banner` in the SAME file (lines 26-31), which correctly uses `role="status" aria-live="polite"` for its own dynamic content. Confirmed by reading the component source directly (not inferred from the DOM captures, since none of the 4 numbered states scroll to reveal this section on screen anyway per D-002).
findings.fix_hint: Add `role="status" aria-live="polite"` to the `.kiosk-waiting-meta` / `.kiosk-waiting-almost-ready` wrapper(s) in KioskWaitingComponent.vue, mirroring the existing kiosk-rush-banner pattern in the same file.

findings.evidence: Every state where the QR is present logs a report-only CSP violation: 'Loading the image http://127.0.0.1:8766/api/frontend/order/track-qr/... violates ... img-src 'self' data: blob: https:'. This is because trackQrUrl (KioskWaitingComponent.vue:274-277) builds an absolute cross-origin URL from `ENV.API_URL`, which in this local/e2e environment is plain http on a different port (8766) than the page origin (8000). Assessed as low-risk/informational: (1) CSP mode is report_only by default (config/security.php:26, CSP_ENFORCE_MODE env) and not blocking; (2) img-src already includes a blanket `https:` scheme-source, so in a real production deployment served over HTTPS end-to-end this would already pass even cross-origin, unlike the earlier C-004 (2026-05-10) storage-URL incident this pattern superficially resembles (config/filesystems.php:43-49), which was specifically about a plain-http same-origin mismatch. Not blocking, but worth a mention given the project's history with this exact CSP directive class.
findings.fix_hint: No action required unless CSP_ENFORCE_MODE is ever flipped to 'enforce' while any deployment target still serves the kiosk API over plain HTTP -- worth a smoke-test note for that cutover, not a Wave D blocker.
